newsitem.title: LEBANON: Banque Audi to list 4,158,000 shares in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Banque Audi to list 4,158,000 shares in Beirut.

text.p: Banque Audi, the second Lebanese commercial bank to list on the Beirut Stock Exchange (BSE), will offer all its 4,158,000 C shares for trading on the market as of next Monday, January 20, the BSE said on Thursday.

"The number of C shares offered for trading in the official market of the Beirut bourse is 4,158,000 nonimal shares. They represent 30 percent of the bank's total number of shares at this date," the BSE said in a statement.
A law passed last year allows Lebanese banks to list and trade 30 percent of their shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange without prior permission from the central bank.
The BSE said Banque Audi's capital of 27.7 billion Lebanese pounds was divided into C shares, 4,620,000 nominal A shares and 5,082,000 B shares.

The C shares were divided into 1,458,000 shares held by the public and 2,700,000 shares in a trust to cover the bank's Global Depositary Receipts -- a $34 million issue in October 1995 raised among international institutional investors.
"GDRs have been issued for the C shares and they are traded on the OTC market of the London Stock Exchange. Each GDR can be converted into one nominal C share," BSE added.
A Beirut dealer said the GDRs were trading $14-$14.5 at the Luxembourg bourse at present.
No price has not been set yet for Audi's shares, which the BSE said have a nominal value of 2,000 Lebanese pounds each.

The BSE said yesterday that it approved on January 9 a request by Banque Audi to list its shares -- the second Lebanese commercial bank to list on the market in a little over two weeks -- and trading would begin on January 20.

Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce was the first bank to list its shares on the exchange since it reopened last year after a 13-year shutdown due to Lebanon's civil war. BLC shares have been the star performer on the market since they began trading on December 30.

At least one other leading Beirut bank, Byblos Bank, is expected to list its shares soon. Dealers say they expect the bank shares to invigorate the stock exchange which has been mostly lacklustre since it reopened in January 1996.
